title: What is the cheapest payment-and-audit protocol that makes honest ML training an equilibrium?
lede: research programme (proposal stage): incentive-compatible verification of outsourced ML training that combines refereed audits, proper scores and peer prediction under floating-point drift, with 17 checked references, hypotheses H1 to H6 and ACM EC as the target venue
summary: An open research programme rather than a finished project. A requester pays untrusted workers to train a model; cheating is cheap and the product cannot be checked without redoing the work. The programme asks for the cheapest protocol that makes full-effort training an equilibrium when the checks are a refereed re-execution of a disputed step, a noisy proper score of the final model on held-out data, and agreement among redundant workers, and when honest workers disagree by floating-point drift. It consolidates about 60 stylised projects in this repository (verification-game, audit-allocation, verifier-bribery, effort-elicitation, reproducible-refereed-training and others). Planned: the drift tolerance priced as a cheating margin, a joint contract over audit rate, stake and score with a proved cost frontier, the stake needed against workers who share one cheap trajectory, and measurement on real small-model training. No results yet: the proposal and log record the plan and the hypotheses before any experiment is run.
